title: Burger Palace
fit_question: Tell me about your most rewarding professional accomplishment and your most difficult professional challenge.
prompt: Burger Palace, a Chicago fast-food chain with 20 locations, has been invited to open inside Midway Airport's main terminal. The CEO wants to know whether it would be profitable. How would you structure the analysis?

clarifying_info.answer: Open if profitable, and act quickly.
Average transaction is $10; variable costs are 80% of revenue; rent and fixed operating cost are $200,000/year and airport royalty is $80,000/year.
Seven current restaurants split demand equally; with Burger Palace, eight would split equally and total customers would not change.

interviewer_notes: Straightforward candidate-led profitability case. Make the candidate structure passenger and employee demand rather than handing over totals. Optional extension calculates breakeven share.

suggested_framework.summary: Book framework covering profitability, airport market and execution risks.

stages.interviewer_asks: How would you assess the location?
stages.expected_answer: Estimate passenger and employee customers, share and ticket size; apply contribution margin and fixed costs; then test competition, preferences, airport execution and strategic fit.

stages.info_to_release: Open 6am-10pm, 350 days; 25 gates, one 175-seat plane/hour/gate, 80% load; 5% of passengers eat. Airport has 2,000 employees and 60% eat daily. Burger Palace gets 1/8 share. Ticket $10, contribution margin 20%, fixed cost $280K.
stages.expected_answer: 400 planes/day×140 passengers=56,000 passengers; 5% eat and 1/8 choose Burger Palace=350/day. Employees add 2,000×60%×1/8=150/day. At 500 customers/day, annual contribution is 500×$10×20%×350=$350K; after $280K fixed cost, profit is $70K.

stages.interviewer_asks: What minimum market share breaks even?
stages.info_to_release: Total daily dining market is 2,800 passengers plus 1,200 employees; average transaction $10; 350 days; contribution margin 20%; fixed costs $280K.
stages.expected_answer: Market revenue is 4,000×$10×350=$14M. Contribution pool is $2.8M. Required share is $280K/$2.8M=10%, below expected 12.5%.
good_answer_signals: Divides fixed cost by contribution pool

stages.expected_answer: Yes: expected profit is $70K and 12.5% expected share exceeds the 10% breakeven share. Validate cuisine/location and share assumptions, costs and royalty; explore airport pricing and brand benefits.

synthesis: Open the Midway restaurant. Expected annual profit is $70K, and expected 12.5% share exceeds 10% breakeven share. Confirm restaurant mix, location, share and cost assumptions and test airport price premiums before committing.
common_pitfalls: Uses plane capacity without load factor
Confuses airport diners with Burger Palace customers

extraction.notes: No candidate exhibit pages; all data are interviewer-released. Reviewed and accepted by Claude 2026-09-30.
